record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.original_question: For a positive integer n >= 2, let C(n) be the maximum number of touching pairs among packings of n congruent unit balls in Euclidean 3-space E^3. For which n can C(n) be achieved by a packing of n unit balls consisting of parallel layers, where each layer is a subset of the densest infinite hexagonal layer of unit balls?

evidence.quote: For a given positive integer n >= 2 find the largest number C(n) of touching pairs in a packing of n congruent balls in E3. Problem 1. Find those positive integers n for which C(n) can be achieved in a packing of n unit balls in E3 consisting of parallel layers of unit balls each being a subset of the densest infinite hexagonal layer of unit balls.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n\ge 2$, consider packings of $n$ congruent closed unit balls in Euclidean 3-space $\mathbb{E}^3$ (so the balls have pairwise disjoint interiors). A touching pair in such a packing is an unordered pair of balls whose boundary spheres are tangent. Let
$$C(n) = \max\{\text{number of touching pairs} : \text{packing of } n \text{ unit balls in } \mathbb{E}^3\}.$$

A hexagonal layer of unit balls is a set of unit balls whose centers lie in a common plane and form a subset of the vertices of a triangular lattice of edge length $2$ in that plane (this is the densest planar arrangement of non-overlapping unit disks of equal radius lying in a plane). A layered packing is a packing of unit balls obtained by stacking finitely many parallel hexagonal layers so that the union is a packing of $\mathbb{E}^3$ (consecutive layers are placed at the minimal admissible distance and each layer is positioned over a deep hole pattern of the previous one).

Determine all positive integers $n\ge 2$ for which the maximum $C(n)$ is attained by some layered packing of $n$ unit balls, i.e. a packing consisting of parallel layers, each layer being a subset of a densest infinite hexagonal layer of unit balls.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Bezdek and collaborators (2012–2021) has produced upper bounds of the form C(n) < 6n - cn^{2/3} and matching lower bounds from layered hexagonal constructions for specific values of n (e.g. n = k(2k²+1)/3), but the exact characterization of those n for which C(n) is achieved by a layered hexagonal packing remains unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Contact graphs of unit sphere packings revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Bezdek-Reid bounds on touching pairs; layered hexagonal constructions used for lower bounds on C(n).
status_evidence.claim: Bounds 0.695 < (6n - C(n))/n^{2/3} < 7.862 hold for special n from hexagonal layered packings, but exact equality cases are not characterized.

status_evidence.title: On contact numbers of locally separable unit sphere packings
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work (2020/2021) continues to address contact number problems in 3-space without resolving the layered-extremality characterization.
status_evidence.claim: The question of which n admit a layered extremal packing remains open.
